name: Can shower valves, showerheads, and drains be moved to a different wall?

mainEntity.name: Can shower valves, showerheads, and drains be moved to a different wall?

acceptedAnswer.text: Moving plumbing lines is common during bathroom remodeling, but it increases the project scope and labor. Relocating a shower valve or adding a secondary handheld sprayer within the same wall cavity is straightforward. However, moving the drain pipe to a new position or shifting the shower to an opposite wall requires cutting into subfloors or concrete slabs to run new waste and vent lines. If your home has a concrete slab foundation, rerouting underground pipes requires trenching, which adds time and expense compared to homes with accessible crawl spaces.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, valves, showerheads, and drains can be relocated, though moving drain lines in concrete slab foundations requires trenching and adds labor.
